الأنهار is its fāʿil, and من تحتها: the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) تجري; the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of جنات, in the position of the accusative. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ إن, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَفْعَلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the khabar of إن. ﴿ما﴾ relative, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يُرِيدُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is a ṣila with no grammatical position. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a jussive-governing conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿كانَ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun omitted, its implied form being هو. ﴿يَظُنُّ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the khabar of كان. ﴿أَنْ﴾ lightened from the heavy أنّ, its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). ﴿لَنْ﴾ an accusative-governing particle. ﴿يَنْصُرَهُ اللَّهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative, and its fronted object, and the Name of Majesty is its postponed fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of أن, and أن and what follows it, as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), fill the place of the two objects of يظن. ﴿فِي الدُّنْيا﴾ the two are attached to ينصره. ﴿وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ conjoined to الدنيا, genitive (majrūr) like it. ﴿فَلْيَمْدُدْ﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis, the lām is the lām of command, and the imperfect verb is jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; the fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the clause of condition and apodosis is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of من. ﴿بِسَبَبٍ﴾ that is, the rope; and السماء here is the ceiling — i.e. whoever despairs of the mercy of Allah, let him hang himself and see whether that brings him any benefit; the two are attached to يمدد. ﴿إِلَى السَّماءِ﴾ the two are attached to يمدد. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لْيَقْطَعْ﴾ its parsing is like ليمدد, and the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرْ﴾ its parsing is like the preceding one. ﴿هَلْ﴾ an interrogative particle. ﴿يُذْهِبَنَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis. ﴿كَيْدُهُ﴾ fāʿil, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ما﴾ relative, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the mafʿūl bihi of ينظر. ﴿يَغِيظُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is a ṣila with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:16-17.t: ﴿وَكَذلِكَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, the kāf is for comparison and ذا is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive by the kāf; the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun). ﴿أَنْزَلْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is resumptive. ﴿آياتٍ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿بَيِّناتٍ﴾ a naʿt, genitive (majrūr) like the noun it qualifies. [Translator's note: so in the source; as a naʿt of the accusative آيات it is accusative, with the kasra.] ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ أن, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; its clause is conjoined to the hāʾ in أنزلناه. ﴿يَهْدِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ owing to heaviness. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of أن. ﴿يُرِيدُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, the noun of إن. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined to the الذين before it. ﴿هادُوا﴾ conjoined to what precedes, and its parsing is like it. ﴿وَالصَّابِئِينَ﴾ they are the worshippers of the stars; conjoined to the noun of إن, accusative with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿وَالنَّصارى﴾ conjoined to الذين; it is accusative like it, with an implied fatḥa on the alif owing to impossibility (taʿadhdhur). ﴿وَالْمَجُوسَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun whose position is the accusative, like what it is conjoined to. ﴿أَشْرَكُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ إن, and the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿يَفْصِلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar. ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place attached to يفصل, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time attached to يفصل. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause إن الله etc. is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the first إن. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty is the noun of إن. ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to the khabar. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿شَهِيدٌ﴾ the khabar of إن, nominative; the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿أَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation, and لم is a particle of negation, jussive government and conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning]. ﴿تَرَ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by deletion of the weak letter, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being أنت; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty is the noun of أن, and أن and what follows it fill the place of the two objects of تر. ﴿يَسْجُدُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). ﴿لَهُ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) يسجد. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of يسجد. ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes. ﴿وَالشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ وَالنُّجُومُ وَالْجِبالُ وَالشَّجَرُ وَالدَّوَابُّ وَكَثِيرٌ﴾ conjoined to the first من. ﴿مِنَ النَّاسِ﴾ the two are attached to كثير. ﴿وَكَثِيرٌ﴾ the wāw is resumptive and كثير is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿حَقَّ﴾ a past verb. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ the two are attached to حق. ﴿الْعَذابُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of كثير, and the clause of the mubtadaʾ and its khabar is resumptive. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; من is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of the accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يُهِنِ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by من; it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and it is given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. [Translator's note: the source heads it with a fatḥa (اللَّهَ); as fāʿil it is ﴿اللَّهُ﴾, as in the verse.] ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis, and ما is negating. ﴿لَهُ﴾ the two are attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. [Translator's note: the verse reads ﴿مِنْ﴾; the source writes مَنْ.] ﴿مُكْرِمٍ﴾ a noun genitive in form, nominative in position as the postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) because it is joined to the fāʾ. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty is the noun of إن, accusative (manṣūb); the clause is resumptive. [Translator's note: the verse reads ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾, as the source's analysis assumes.] ﴿يَفْعَلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being هو. ﴿ما﴾ relative, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of إن. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the ṣila.

daas-irab:19-21.t: ﴿هذانِ﴾ the hā is for calling attention (tanbīh), and ذان is a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). [Translator's note: so in the source; ذان is more commonly described as nominative with the alif, as a dual.] ﴿خَصْمانِ﴾ khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ) with the alif because it is a dual; the clause is resumptive. ﴿اخْتَصَمُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of خصمان. ﴿فِي رَبِّهِمْ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) اختصموا, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَالَّذِينَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and الذين is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position. ﴿قُطِّعَتْ لَهُمْ ثِيابٌ﴾ a passive past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine; ثياب is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and لهم: the two are attached to قطعت; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنْ نارٍ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted naʿt of ثياب. ﴿يُصَبُّ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿مِنْ فَوْقِ﴾ the two are attached to يصب. ﴿رُؤُسِهِمُ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الْحَمِيمُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is resumptive or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in لهم. ﴿يُصْهَرُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two are attached to يصهر. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿فِي بُطُونِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ṣila, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْجُلُودُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; الجلود is conjoined to ما and is nominative like it. ﴿وَلَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and لهم: the two are attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿مَقامِعُ﴾ postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ حَدِيدٍ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted naʿt of مقامع.

daas-irab:22-24.t: ﴿كُلَّما﴾ an adverb containing the meaning of condition. ﴿أَرادُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿أَنْ﴾ accusative-governing. ﴿يَخْرُجُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, the sign of its accusative being the deletion of the nūn; the clause, as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of أرادوا. ﴿مِنْها﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) يخرجوا. ﴿مِنْ غَمٍّ﴾ the two are attached to يخرجوا. ﴿أُعِيدُوا﴾ a passive past verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of كلما. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to أعيدوا. ﴿وَذُوقُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and ذوقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of the omitted verb قيل. ﴿عَذابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْحَرِيقِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ إن, and the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿يُدْخِلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being هو; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of إن. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾ conjoined to it, and its parsing is like it. ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, accusative with the kasra in place of the fatḥa because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ owing to heaviness. ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ the two are attached to تجري. ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of جنات. ﴿يُحَلَّوْنَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ أَساوِرَ﴾ من is redundant (zāʾida), and أساور is mafʿūl bihi, genitive (majrūr) with the fatḥa because it is a diptote, accusative in position. ﴿مِنْ ذَهَبٍ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted naʿt of أساور. ﴿وَلُؤْلُؤاً﴾ conjoined to the position of من أساور, or the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being ويؤتون. ﴿وَلِباسُهُمْ فِيها حَرِيرٌ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar; the clause is resumptive, and فيها: the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَهُدُوا﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and هدوا is a passive past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is joined to the wāw of the group; the wāw is an attached pronoun, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِلَى الطَّيِّبِ﴾ the two are attached to هدوا. ﴿مِنَ الْقَوْلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from الطيب. ﴿وَهُدُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and هدوا is a passive past verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿إِلى صِراطِ﴾ the two are attached to هدوا. ﴿الْحَمِيدِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the preceding one.

daas-irab:25-26.t: ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the noun of إن; the clause is resumptive. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is joined to the wāw of the group, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position. ﴿وَيَصُدُّونَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to كفروا. ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) يصدون. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالْمَسْجِدِ﴾ conjoined to سبيل. ﴿الْحَرامِ﴾ a naʿt (adjective). ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a relative noun in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of, or badal (substitute) from, المسجد. ﴿جَعَلْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first object; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿لِلنَّاسِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿سَواءً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or a ḥāl if the verb is taken as not transitive to two objects. ﴿الْعاكِفُ﴾ fāʿil of سواء. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ the two are attached to العاكف. ﴿وَالْبادِ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and الباد is conjoined to العاكف. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and من is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive. ﴿يُرِدْ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿فِيهِ﴾ the two are attached to يرد. ﴿بِإِلْحادٍ﴾ the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and إلحاد is genitive in form, accusative in position as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بِظُلْمٍ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted naʿt of إلحاد. ﴿نُذِقْهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), its fāʿil latent, its implied form being نحن, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the two clauses of condition and apodosis are in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of من. ﴿مِنْ عَذابٍ﴾ the two are attached to نذقه. ﴿أَلِيمٍ﴾ a naʿt of عذاب, genitive (majrūr) like it. ﴿وَإِذْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and إذ is an adverb of time attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكر. ﴿بَوَّأْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿لِإِبْراهِيمَ﴾ the two are attached to بوأنا. ﴿مَكانَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْبَيْتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿ألا﴾ أن assimilated into لا; it is explicative (tafsīriyya). ﴿لا﴾ prohibitive. ﴿تُشْرِكْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by لا, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being أنت. ﴿بِي﴾ the two are attached to تشرك. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); the clause has no grammatical position because it is explicative. ﴿وَطَهِّرْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being أنت; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بَيْتِيَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ of the speaker, its appearance prevented by the place being occupied by the suitable vowel, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لِلطَّائِفِينَ﴾ the two are attached to طهر. ﴿وَالْقائِمِينَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and القائمين is a conjoined noun, genitive like it with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿وَالرُّكَّعِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes. ﴿السُّجُودِ﴾ a naʿt, genitive with the kasra.

daas-irab:27-29.t: ﴿وَأَذِّنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; أذن is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being أنت; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to what precedes. ﴿فِي النَّاسِ﴾ ﴿بِالْحَجِّ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) أذن. ﴿يَأْتُوكَ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by deletion of the nūn because it is the response to the command (jawāb al-ṭalab); the wāw is the fāʿil and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the response to the command. ﴿رِجالًا﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is "on foot". ﴿وَعَلى كُلِّ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to an omitted ḥāl, its implied form being وركبانا على كل, and it is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ضامِرٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿يَأْتِينَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by retention of the nūn, and the yāʾ is the fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of ضامر. [Translator's note: so in the source; in يأتين the nūn is that of the feminine plural and is itself the fāʿil, the verb being indeclinable on the sukūn.] ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ﴾ the two are attached to يأتين. ﴿فَجٍّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; it means "road". ﴿عَمِيقٍ﴾ a naʿt; together they mean "distant". ﴿لِيَشْهَدُوا﴾ the lām is the lām of causation (taʿlīl), and the imperfect verb is accusative (manṣūb) by the implied (muḍmara) أن after the lām of causation, [marked] by deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive, [and with the lām] the two are attached to أذن. ﴿مَنافِعَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to منافع. ﴿وَيَذْكُرُوا﴾ the clause is conjoined to يشهدوا, and its parsing is like it. ﴿اسْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فِي أَيَّامٍ﴾ the two are attached to يذكروا. ﴿معدودات﴾ a naʿt of أيام, genitive (majrūr) with the kasra. ﴿عَلى﴾ a preposition. ﴿ما﴾ relative; the two are attached to يذكروا. ﴿رَزَقَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent, and the hāʾ is its object and the mīm is for the group; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنْ بَهِيمَةِ﴾ the two are attached to رزقهم. ﴿الْأَنْعامِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَكُلُوا﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it occurs as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿مِنْها﴾ the two are attached to كلوا. ﴿وَأَطْعِمُوا﴾ the clause is conjoined, and its parsing is like it. ﴿الْبائِسَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْفَقِيرَ﴾ a naʿt, accusative. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لْيَقْضُوا﴾ the lām is the lām of command, and the imperfect verb is jussive by the lām of command, [marked] by deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿تَفَثَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلْيُوفُوا﴾ its parsing is like ليقضوا, and it is conjoined to it. ﴿نُذُورَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلْيَطَّوَّفُوا﴾ like وليوفوا, conjoined. ﴿بِالْبَيْتِ﴾ the two are attached to يطوفوا. ﴿الْعَتِيقِ﴾ a naʿt.

farraa:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدَافِعُ﴾ — and (يَدْفع) also. Most of the Readers read (يدافع), and that is how I read. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read (يدافع), and (وَلَو لاَ دِفَاعُ الله); and each of them is correct.

farraa:39-39.t: His saying: ﴿أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقَاتَلُونَ﴾ — also (يقاتِلوُن). Its meaning is: Allah has given permission to those who fight, that they may fight; this was when ﴿فَاقْتُلوُا المُشْرِكينَ حيثُ وَجَدْتُمُوهُمْ﴾ was revealed. It was also read ﴿أذن للذين يقاتلون بأنهم ظلموا﴾, and the meaning is: permission has been given them to fight. Each of them is correct.

farraa:40-40.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُواْ مِن دِيَارِهِم بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ﴾ — He is saying: they were expelled only for their saying "There is no god but Allah". If you wish, you may make His saying ﴿لاَّ أَن يَقُولُواْ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ﴾ in the position of the genitive (khafḍ), referring it back to the bāʾ in (بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ); and if you wish, you may make (أن) the excepted (mustathnā), as He said: ﴿إلاَّ ابْتغاء وَجْهِ ربِّه الأعلى﴾.
His saying: ﴿لَّهُدِّمَتْ صَوَامِعُ وَبِيَعٌ﴾ — these [the biyaʿ] are the places of prayer of the Christians, and the ṣawāmiʿ (cloisters) are for the monks. As for the ṣalawāt, they are the synagogues of the Jews, and the masājid are (the mosques of Islam). The meaning of the demolishing is that Allah said before that: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ﴾ — He repels, by His command and by its followers, [harm] from the religion of every prophet, until Allah sent Muḥammad ﷺ.

farraa:45-45.t: His saying: ﴿فَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا وَبِئْرٍ مُّعَطَّلَةٍ وَقَصْرٍ مَّشِيدٍ﴾ — the well and the palace are put in the genitive (khafḍ) by conjunction (ʿaṭf) with the roofs (العروش). Yet when you consider its meaning, you find that (عَلَى) does not fit well with them, because the roofs are the tops of the houses, whereas the well is in the ground, and likewise the palace, since the town did not collapse onto the palace. Rather, one part was made to follow another, as He said: ﴿وَحُورٍ عينٍ كأَمْثَالِ اللُؤْلُؤ﴾. And if you put the well «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 122b]» and the palace in the genitive — intending that they are not part of the town — by means of من, it would be as if you said: How many a town has been destroyed, and how many a well and how many a palace. The first is dearer to me.

farraa:46-46.t: His saying: ﴿فَإِنَّهَا لاَ تَعْمَى ٱلأَبْصَارُ﴾ — the hāʾ is (a hāʾ of ʿimād, a support pronoun) by which إنّ is given its due. (إنَّه) is permissible in its place, and that is the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (فانه لا تعمى الأبصَار ولكن تعمى القلوب التى فى الصّدور). The heart is only ever in the breast; it is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the kind the Arabs add to a meaning already known, as it was said: ﴿فصِيَامُ ثَلاَثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فى الحَجِّ وسَبْعَةٍ إذا رَجَعتُم تِلْكَ عَشَرةٌ كامِلَةٌ﴾, and it is known that three and seven make ten. Similar to that is: "I looked at you with my own eye". Similar to it is the saying of Allah: ﴿يَقُولُونَ بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ مَا لَيْسَ فِى قُلُوبِهِم﴾, and in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: ﴿إنَّ هَذَا أَخِى لَهُ تِسْعٌ وَتِسْعٌ وَتِسْعُون نَعْجَةً وَلِى نَعْجَةٌ أٌنْثَى﴾; this too is emphasis. And if someone says: ﴿كيف انْصرَف من العذاب﴾ «[Translator's note: i.e. "How did it turn away from the punishment"]» to the point where He said: ﴿وإنَّ يوماً عند رَبِّك﴾? The answer to that is that they sought to hasten the punishment in this world, so Allah revealed to His Prophet: ﴿وَلَنْ يُخْلِفَ اللهُ وَعْدَهُ﴾, that is, in sending the punishment down upon them in this world. So His saying ﴿وَإِنَّ يَوْماً عند رَبِّك﴾ is also about their punishment. Thus it is consistent: they are punished in this world, and in the Hereafter more severely.

farraa:47-47.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّ يَوْماً عِندَ رَبِّكَ كَأَلْفِ سَنَةٍ مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ﴾.
It is said: a day of the days of their punishment in the Hereafter is like a thousand years of what you count in this world.

farraa:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿مُعَاجِزِينَ﴾ — the reading of the general public is (مُعَاجِزِينَ), and the meaning of muʿājizīn is "obstinately opposing". The entry of (فى) is as when you say: "I strove in your affair", meaning: I intended good or evil for you. Mujāhid and ʿAbdallāh ibn al-Zubayr read (معجِّزينَ), meaning: hindering [others].

farraa:52-52.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ وَلاَ نَبِيٍّ إِلاَّ﴾ — the messenger (rasūl) is the prophet who is sent, and the prophet (nabī) is the one spoken to [by inspiration] who has not been sent.
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ إِذَا تَمَنَّىٰ﴾ — al-tamannī is recitation, and also talking to oneself.

farraa:63-63.t:
His saying: ﴿فَتُصْبِحُ ٱلأَرْضُ مُخْضَرَّةً﴾ — you put (فتُصبح) in the nominative (rafʿ) because the meaning of ﴿أَلَم تر﴾ is a statement (khabar), as though you said in ordinary speech: Know that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes [green]. It is like the poet's saying:
أَلم تسأل الربع القديم فينطق * فهل تُخبرنكَ اليوم بَيْداءٌ سَمْلَق
(Did you not ask the old encampment, and it speaks? — but will a barren desert tell you anything today?)
that is: you have asked it, and it spoke. Had you made it a question and made the fāʾ [introduce] a condition, you would put it in the accusative (naṣb), as another said:
أَلَم تسأل فتخبرَك الديارا * عن الحىّ المضلَّل حيث سَارَا
(Will you not ask, so that the abodes may tell you of the misguided tribe, where it has gone?)
The jussive (jazm) is also permissible in this verse, as he said:
فقلت له صَوِّب ولا تجهدَنَّه * فيُذرك من أخرى العَطاةِ فَتزلق
(I said to him: "Bring it down gently and do not overtax it, lest it throw you from the rear of the [mount] and you slip.")
for he made the answer with the fāʾ as though it were coordinated with what precedes it.

farraa:67-67.t: His saying: ﴿مَنسَكاً﴾ and ﴿مَنْسِكاً﴾ — it has been read both ways. Mansik is [the usage] of the people of the Ḥijāz and mansak of the Banū Asad. Al-mansak in the speech of the Arabs is the place you frequent habitually and are attached to; it is said: "So-and-so has a mansik that he frequents", whether in good or otherwise. The rites (al-manāsik) were named after that — and Allah knows best — because people keep returning to them for the Ḥajj and the ʿUmra.

farraa:72-72.t:
His saying: ﴿يَكَادُونَ يَسْطُونَ بِٱلَّذِينَ يَتْلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ آيَٰتِنَا﴾ — He means the idolaters of the people of Mecca: whenever they heard a man «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 213a]» of the Muslims reciting the Qurʾān, they nearly assaulted him.
His saying: ﴿ٱلنَّارُ وَعَدَهَا ٱللَّهُ﴾ — you put it in the nominative because it is a definite noun explaining الشرّ (the worse), which is indefinite; as you say: "I passed by two men — your father and your brother". Had you put it in the accusative by means of what refers back to it [the pronoun in وعدها], intending to connect it with what precedes, it would be a valid way. And had you put it in the genitive by the bāʾ — ﴿فأنبئكم بشرّ من ذلكم بالنار﴾ — it would be correct. But the [preferred] way is the nominative.

farraa:73-73.t: His saying: ﴿ٱلطَّالِبُ وَٱلْمَطْلُوبُ﴾ — the seeker is the gods, and the sought is the fly. It carries the sense of a parable.

farraa:74-74.t: His saying: ﴿مَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ﴾ — that is, they did not magnify Allah as He truly deserves to be magnified. It is as you say in ordinary speech: "You did not recognise so-and-so's worth (qadr)", that is, his greatness, and his companion fell short in his regard.

farraa:75-75.t: His saying: ﴿ٱللَّهُ يَصْطَفِي مِنَ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةِ رُسُلاً﴾ — He chose from among them Jibrīl, Mīkāʾīl, the Angel of Death and their like; and He chooses from among mankind the prophets.

farraa:77-77.t: His saying: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱرْكَعُواْ وَٱسْجُدُواْ﴾ — people used to prostrate without bowing, so they were commanded that their prayer should have a bowing before the prostration.

farraa:78-78.t:
His saying: ﴿فِي ٱلدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ﴾ — [ḥaraj means] constriction.
His saying: ﴿مِّلَّةَ أَبِيكُمْ﴾ — you put it in the accusative on the sense: He has made it wide for you like the religion (milla) of your father Ibrāhīm; because His saying ﴿وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي ٱلدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ﴾ means: He made it wide and easy like the religion of Ibrāhīm; so when you drop the kāf, you put it in the accusative. ﴿مِلَّةَ إبراهيم﴾ may also be put in the accusative as a command to [follow] it, because the beginning of the passage is a command, as though He said: Bow, and hold fast to the religion of Ibrāhīm.
His saying: ﴿مِن قَبْلُ وَفِي هَـٰذَا﴾ — He means the Qurʾān.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying: ﴿تَذْهَلُ كُلُّ مُرْضِعَةٍ﴾: the readers put (كلُّ مُرْضِعَة) in the nominative because they made the verb belong to it. Had it been said "tudhhilu kulla murḍiʿatin" (accusative), meaning that the Hour makes its people distracted, it would have been a valid option, but I have not heard anyone read it so. Al-murḍiʿa is the mother; al-murḍiʿ is the woman who has a child with her whom she suckles. Were murḍiʿ said of the mother — since suckling only comes from females — it would be like your saying ṭāmith and ḥāʾiḍ ("menstruating", without the feminine ending). And had murḍiʿa been said of the one who has a child with her, it would have been correct.
His saying: ﴿وَتَرَى ٱلنَّاسَ سُكَارَىٰ وَمَا هُم بِسُكَارَىٰ﴾: the people and the readers agreed on (سُكَارَى ومَاهُمْ بِسُكَارى). Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Hushaym narrated to me from Mughīra from Ibrāhīm from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he read (وَتَرى الناسَ سَكْرَى وَمَا هُمْ بِسَكْرَى), and that is a good option in Arabic (because it is on a par with al-halkā and al-jarḥā ("the perishing", "the wounded"), and not in the manner of al-nashwān and al-nashāwā ("tipsy")). The Arabs take fāʿil, faʿīl and faʿil, when the one so described is like the sick, the felled or the wounded, and pluralize it on the pattern faʿlā; they made faʿlā a mark of the plural of everyone afflicted with chronic illness, harm or perishing, and they do not care whether its singular [Translator's note: the text has «واحه», evidently for «واحده»] is fāʿil, faʿīl or faʿlān. So sakrā, dropping the alif, was chosen because of the terror and fright of that Day. Had it been said (sakrā) on the basis that the plural takes the feminine and so is like a singular feminine, it would have been a valid option, as Allah said: ﴿وللهِ الأسْماءُ الحُسنَى﴾ and ﴿والقُرونَ الأُولَى﴾; and al-nās are a collective, so it is permissible for that to apply to them. The Arabs have said: "qad jāʾatka al-nās" ("the people have come to you", feminine verb). One of them recited to me:
أضحت بنو عامر غَضْبَى أنوفُهم * أَنّى عفوت فلا عارٌ ولا باس
(The Banū ʿĀmir became angry, their noses bristling, because I pardoned; yet there is no shame and no harm.)
He said ghaḍbā for "the noses", in the way I have explained to you.
It is mentioned that one of the readers read (وَتُرَى الناسَ), and that is a good option. He means something like your saying "ruʾīta annaka qāʾim" and "ruʾītuka qāʾiman" ("you were seen to be standing"); you make (سكارى) be in the position of the accusative, because (تُرَى) needs two things which it puts in the accusative, as verbs of thinking (al-ẓann) need.

farraa:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ﴾: the hāʾ in (عَلَيه) and in (أَنَّهُ يُضِلُّهُ) refers to the rebellious devil. Its meaning: it has been decreed for him that he will lead astray whoever follows him.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿مُّخَلَّقَةٍ وَغَيْرِ مُخَلَّقَةٍ﴾: He is saying: complete and miscarried. It is permissible [119 b] [Translator's note: to read] mukhallaqatan wa-ghayra mukhallaqatin as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the ḥāl is put in the accusative with definite and indefinite nouns alike, as you say "hal min rajulin yuḍrabu mujarradan?" ("is there a man who is beaten stripped?"). This is a ḥāl and not a naʿt (adjective).
His saying: ﴿لِّنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَنُقِرُّ فِي ٱلأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ﴾: He began (ونُقِرُّ فى الأرحَام) anew and did not refer it back to (لنبيّن). Had (ليُبيِّن) been read, meaning "so that Allah may make clear to you", it would have been correct, but I have not heard it.
His saying: ﴿وَمِنكُمْ مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ﴾: to the lowest stage of life. ﴿لِكَيْلاَ يَعْلَمَ﴾: He is saying: so that he does not understand (anything) after his former understanding.
His saying: (ورَبَت): the readers read (وَرَبَتْ) (from tarbū, "it swells"). Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Tamīmī narrated to me from Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī that he read ﴿¤هْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَأتْ﴾ with hamza. If he took it to be from al-rabīʾa, the one who keeps watch for the people, that is an approach: i.e. it rose until it became like a lookout place for the watchman. If he did not mean (by it) this, then it is one of the mistakes the Arabs sometimes make, saying ḥallaʾtu al-sawīq, labbaʾtu bi-l-ḥajj and rathaʾtu al-mayyit [Translator's note: with a spurious hamza]; it is like al-Ḥasan's reading ﴿وَلأَدْرَأتكم بِهِ﴾ with hamza. It is among what is rejected in recitation.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿ثَانِيَ عِطْفِهِ﴾ is accusative on the sense of: he disputes, turning his side away — averting himself from the Reminder.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَعْبُدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ حَرْفٍ﴾: it was revealed about some Bedouins of the Banū Asad [Translator's note: the text has «أشد»] who moved to Medina with their families, and then made a favour of that to the Prophet ﷺ [Translator's note: the text has «قامتنّوا», evidently for «فامتنّوا»], saying: "A man (after a man) of a tribe embraces Islam, while we have brought you our families." When they were given some of the alms and their livestock and horses remained safe, they said: "What an excellent religion this is!" And if they were not given any of the alms and their livestock did not remain safe, they turned back from Islam. That is His saying ﴿يَعْبُدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ حَرْفٍ فَإِنْ أَصَابَهُ خَيْرٌ ٱطْمَأَنَّ بِهِ﴾: He is saying: he remains in it; ﴿وَإِنْ أَصَابَتْهُ فِتْنَةٌ ٱنْقَلَبَ﴾: and goes back.
His saying: ﴿خَسِرَ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآُخِرَةَ﴾: he has been cheated of both. It is reported of Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj alone that he read (خاسِر الدنيا والآخرة). All is correct, and the meaning is the same.

farraa:12-13.t:
His saying: ﴿يَدْعُو مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ means the idols.
Then He said: ﴿يَدْعُو لَمَنْ ضَرُّهُ﴾, and the exegesis has come as: "he calls upon one whose harm is nearer than his benefit"; the lām has intervened between them. Thus it is in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (يَدْعو من ضَرُّه). We have not found the Arabs saying "ḍarabtu la-akhāka" or "raʾaytu la-Zaydan afḍala minka". Yet the readers have agreed on it. We consider that it is permissible because (مَن) is a word in which the case-ending does not show; so it was permitted — [Translator's note: manuscript] B: so it was deemed permissible — to interpose the lām before the noun, since the case-ending does not show in it. It is reported of the Arabs that they said "ʿindī la-mā ghayruhu khayrun minhu" ("I have what something other than it is better than"), interposing the lām before what makes [Translator's note: the predicate] nominative, whereas the lām's place should have been in (ḍarruhu), and in your saying "ʿindī mā la-ghayruhu khayrun minhu". This is the explanation of the reading, out of following [Translator's note: the received text]. And it may be that His saying is: ﴿ذَلِكَ هُوَ الضَّلالُ البَعِيدُ يَدْعُو﴾, so that you make (يدعو) part of the ṣila (relative clause) of (al-ḍalālu al-baʿīd), implying the hāʾ in (يدعو), and then begin the speech anew with the lām, saying (لمَنْ ضَرُّهُ أقربُ مِن نَفْعِهِ لَبِئسَ المَوْلَي), like your saying, in the conditional manner, "la-mā faʿalta la-huwa khayrun laka" ("what you have done is surely better for you"). That is a strong option in Arabic.
And there is another option that has not been read: that you give kasra to the lām in (لمن), meaning "he calls to one [120 a] whose harm is nearer than his benefit", so that the lām is on a par with ilā, as He said ﴿الحَمْدُ لِلّهِ الذِى هَدَانا لِهَذَا﴾, i.e. "to this" (ilā hādhā). You say in speech: "daʿawtu ilā fulān" and "daʿawtu li-fulān" with one meaning. Were it not for the dislike of departing from the transmitted reports and the consensus, it would have been a good option of reading. His saying (يَدْعو) that comes after (al-baʿīd) would then be a repetition of His saying ﴿يدعو من دون الله﴾ — yadʿū repeated, as you say "he calls, he calls, persistently". This is a support for whoever gives the lām fatḥa [Translator's note: the text has «نضب», evidently for «نصب»] and does not make (يدعو) fall on (مَنْ). Al-ḍalāl al-baʿīd is the long [Translator's note: straying].

farraa:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿مَن كَانَ يَظُنُّ أَن لَّن يَنصُرَهُ ٱللَّهُ﴾ is a condition whose apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is in His saying ﴿فَلْيَمْدُدْ بِسَبَبٍ﴾. The hāʾ in (His saying) ﴿يَنصُرَهُ ٱللَّهُ﴾ refers to the Prophet ﷺ; i.e. whoever of you thinks that Allah will not help Muḥammad to victory so that he makes the religion of Allah prevail, let him put a rope in the ceiling of his house and then strangle himself with it. That is His saying ﴿ثُمَّ لْيَقْطَعْ﴾ by strangling. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (ثم ليقطه) [Translator's note: so in the text; probably «ليقطعه» is meant], i.e. the cord, which is the rope. He is saying: ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرْ هَلْ يُذْهِبَنَّ كَيْدُهُ﴾ — when he does that — his rage. (مَا يَغِيظُ) is in the position of the accusative.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ﴾ up to His saying ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوۤاْ﴾, then He said ﴿إِنَّ ¤للَّهَ﴾: He placed (إنَّ) in their khabar (predicate) and (إنَّ) at the beginning of the speech, while you do not say in speech "inna akhāka innahu dhāhib". It is permissible here because the meaning is like a condition: i.e. whoever was a believer or followed any of these religions, the judgement between them and their reckoning rest with Allah. The Arabs sometimes say: "inna akhāka inna al-dayna ʿalayhi la-kathīr" ("your brother — the debt upon him is great"), placing (إنَّ) in its khabar when it is made nominative only by a noun connected to a mention of it [Translator's note: i.e. containing a pronoun referring back to it], as the poet said:
إنَّ الخليفة إن الله سَرْبله * سِرْبال مُلْك به ترجَى الخواتيم
(The caliph — Allah has clothed him with the garment of sovereignty, through which good endings are hoped for.)
Whoever says this does not say "innaka innaka qāʾim", nor "inna abāka innahu qāʾim", because [Translator's note: in the permitted case] the two nouns differ, so it is good to set the first aside and make the second as though it were the mubtadaʾ (subject); it is good when they differ and ugly when they are the same.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ﴾: He means the inhabitants of the heavens; ﴿وَمَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ means every creature — of the mountains, of the jinn, and the like; ﴿وَٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ وَٱلنُّجُومُ وَٱلْجِبَالُ وَٱلشَّجَرُ وَٱلدَّوَآبُّ وَكَثِيرٌ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ﴾ — of the people of obedience. ﴿وَكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْعَذَابُ﴾ indicates that [Translator's note: the meaning is] "and many refused to prostrate", because punishment does not become due upon anyone except for abandoning prostration and obedience. You put it in the nominative by the mention of it that returns in His saying ﴿حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ﴾, so ﴿حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ﴾ is on a par with "refused". Had you used the accusative — "wa-kathīran ḥaqqa [Translator's note: ʿalayhi] al-ʿadhāb" — it would have been a valid option, on a par with His saying ﴿قَرِيقاً هَدَى وفَرِيقاً حَقَّ عليهم الضلالة﴾: the accusative is used when there is a wāw in the phrase and the mention of it returns with a verb that has fallen upon it. The nominative is also possible in it, because of the returning mention, as Allah said ﴿وَالشُّعَرَاءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ الغاوُونَ﴾ and as He said ﴿وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ﴾.
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُ مِن مُّكْرِمٍ﴾: He is saying: whomever Allah makes wretched, he has no one to make him happy. It is also read ﴿فمَا لَه من مُكْرَم﴾, meaning: [Translator's note: no] honouring.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿هَـٰذَانِ خَصْمَانِ ٱخْتَصَمُواْ فِي رَبِّهِمْ﴾: two parties, the people of two religions. One of the two disputants is the Muslims, and the other the Jews [Translator's note: and] the Christians.
His saying: ﴿ٱخْتَصَمُواْ فِي رَبِّهِمْ﴾: about the religion of their Lord. The Jews and the Christians said to the Muslims: "Our religion is better than your religion, because we preceded you." The Muslims said: "Rather, our religion is better than your religion, because we believe in our Prophet and the Qurʾān, and we believe in your prophets and your books, while you disbelieve in our Prophet and our Book." So the Muslims prevailed over them in argument, and Allah revealed this verse.
His saying: ﴿ٱخْتَصَمُواْ﴾: He did not say ikhtaṣamā (dual) because they are two groups, not two men; had ikhtaṣamā been said, it would have been correct. Similar to it is ﴿وَإن طَائِفَتَانِ مِنَ المؤمنِينَ اقتتَلُوا﴾, taking it to refer to the plural; had iqtatalatā been said, it would have been permissible, taking it to refer to the two parties.

farraa:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿يُصْهَرُ بِهِ مَا فِي بُطُونِهِمْ﴾: it is melted by it. You say: ṣahartu the fat with fire ("I melted the fat").

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَهُمْ مَّقَامِعُ مِنْ حَدِيدٍ﴾: it is related that they hope (to get out) of the Fire, until, when they attempt it, the keepers strike [Translator's note: the text has «ضرت», evidently for «ضربت»] their heads with the hooked rods, so that their heads are caved in, and boiling water is poured into their brains and melts the fat of their bellies. That is His saying in [Translator's note: Sūrat] Ibrāhīm ﴿ويُسْقَى مِنْ مَاءٍ صَدِيدٍ﴾, from what melts out of their bellies and their skins.
His saying: ﴿يَتَجَرعُهُ ولا يكادُ يُسيغُهُ﴾: he is forced to it.

farraa:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿وَلُؤْلُؤاً﴾: the people of Medina read this one and the one in al-Malāʾika [Translator's note: i.e. Sūrat Fāṭir] ﴿ولُؤْلُؤاً﴾ with alif [Translator's note: i.e. accusative], and al-Aʿmash read both in the genitive. I saw it in the copies (maṣāḥif) of ʿAbd Allāh — the one in al-Ḥajj specifically — as (ولُؤْلأ) ﴿وَلاَ تَهَجَّأْه﴾ [Translator's note: these two words, "and do not spell it out", appear in the text with Quranic brackets; they seem to be an aside rather than a quotation]. That is because in his copies the hamza is written with alif in every case, whether what precedes it has kasra, fatḥa or anything else. The one in al-Malāʾika is written in our copies (ولؤلؤ) without alif, and the one in al-Ḥajj (ولؤلؤا) with alif; so the genitive and the accusative are both permissible in the two of them. The accusative in the one in al-Ḥajj is better grounded — because of the alif — than in the one in al-Malāʾika.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَيَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: yafʿalūna (imperfect) has been referred back to faʿalū (past) because their meaning is as though one, in alladhī and in what is not alladhī. Had it been said "inna alladhīna kafarū wa-ṣaddū", there would have been nothing in it to ask about. You refer yafʿalūna to faʿalū because you mean: "those who have disbelieved hinder by their disbelief." Your insertion of the wāw is like His saying ﴿وَلِيَرْضَوْهُ وَلِيَقْترِفُوا﴾: you implied a verb in the wāw along with the hindering, just as you implied it there. Or, if you wish, you say: the hindering on their part is as it were continuous, so yafʿalūna was chosen for them, as though you said: "Those who have disbelieved, and whose habit is hindering." Similar to it is ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْفُرونَ بآياتِ اللهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ النبيّينَ﴾, and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ﴿وَقَاتَلُوا الذينَ يأمرونَ بالقِسْطِ﴾. And He said ﴿الذِينَ آمَنُوا وتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾, like that. Similar to it in al-Aḥzāb, in the reading [Translator's note: the text has «قرءاة»] of ʿAbd Allāh: (الذِينَ بَلَّغُوا رِسالات الله وَيَخْشَوْنَه). So there is no harm in referring faʿala back to yafʿalu, as He said ﴿وَقَاتلُوا الذِينَ يأمرونَ﴾, or yafʿalu back to faʿala, as He said ﴿إِنَّ الذينَ كفروا وَيَصُدّون عن سبيل الله﴾.
His saying: ﴿سَوَآءً ٱلْعَاكِفُ فِيهِ وَٱلْبَادِ﴾: al-ʿākif is whoever is of the people of Mecca, and al-bādī is whoever comes to it for ḥajj or ʿumra. The readers agreed on putting (سواء) in the nominative here [Translator's note: the Quranic text printed in this entry is vowelled «سَوَآءً», accusative]. As for His saying [121 a] in al-Sharīʿa [Translator's note: i.e. Sūrat al-Jāthiya]: ﴿سواء مَحْيَاهُمْ وَمَمَاتُهُمْ﴾, al-Aʿmash alone read it in the accusative, and the rest of the readers in the nominative. Whoever uses the accusative makes ﴿جَعَلناه﴾ fall on it; whoever uses the nominative makes the verb fall on the hāʾ and the lām in "for the people", then begins anew and says: ﴿سَوَاءٌ العاكِفُ فِيهِ والبادِ﴾. It is the way of the Arabs to begin anew with sawāʾ when it comes after a word with which the speech is complete; they say: "I passed by a man — alike (sawāʾun) to him are good and evil." The genitive is permissible. They chose the nominative only because (سواء) has the sense of "one", as though you said: "I passed by a man — one (wāḥidun) to him are good and evil." Whoever uses the genitive means "balanced (muʿtadilin) to him are good and evil". They do not say "I passed by a man, muʿtadilun to him are good and evil" (in the nominative), because (muʿtadil) is an explicit verbal form, whereas sawāʾ has the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun). Their treating it as a verbal form is like their treating "I passed by a man, ḥasbika min rajulin" ("sufficient for you as a man") as a verbal form.
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحَادٍ بِظُلْمٍ﴾: the bāʾ entered (ilḥād) because its interpretation is: "whoever intends to deviate in it wrongfully." The entry of the bāʾ with (أن) is easier than with al-ilḥād and the like, because prepositions are often implied with (أن), and it is like a condition, so it tolerates the entry of the preposition and its absence, since the case-ending does not show in it; whereas it is rare with maṣdars, because the nominative and genitive show in them. Abū al-Jarrāḥ recited to me:
فلمَّا رَجَتْ بالشّرب هَزّ لها العصا * شَحِيح له عند الإزاء نَهِيم
(When she hoped for a drink, a stingy man with a growl at the trough's spout shook the stick at her.)
(Al-Farrāʾ said: nahīm is a kind of sound.) And Imruʾ al-Qays said:
ألا هل أتاها والحوادث جَمَّة * بأن امرأ القيس بنَ تَمْلِك بَيْقرا
(Has it reached her — and events are many — that Imruʾ al-Qays son of Tamlik has gone to the towns and settled?)
He put the bāʾ on (أنّ) while it is in the position of the nominative, just as He put it on (ilḥādin bi-ẓulmin) while it is in the position of the accusative. They have also put it — meaning the bāʾ — on (مَا) when they intend it as a maṣdar. Qays ibn Zuhayr said:
ألم يأتيك والأنباءُ تنمِى * بما لاقت لبونُ بنى زيادِ
(Has it not reached you — and news spreads — what the milch-camels of the Banū Ziyād met with?)
It is rarer with (ما) than with (أن), because (أن) resembles nouns less than (مَا) does. I heard a Bedouin of Rabīʿa — I had asked him about something — say: "arjū bi-dhāka" ("I hope for that"), meaning "arjū dhāka". Some of the readers read (وَمَن تَرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحَادٍ), from al-wurūd ("arriving"), as though meaning: "whoever arrives at it or makes his way to it". I do not like it, because waradtu requires a [Translator's note: direct] noun; do you not see that you say "waradnā Makka" and do not say "waradnā fī Makka"? It is permissible if you mean "alighting". It may also be permissible in the dialect of the Ṭayyiʾ, because they say "raghibtu fīka", meaning "raghibtu bika". One of them recited to me about a daughter of his:
وأرغبُ فيهَا عن لَقِيطٍ ورَهْطه * ولكننى عن سِنْبِسٍ لست أرغب
(I hold her too dear for Laqīṭ and his clan, but I do not hold her too dear for Sinbis.)
(He means his daughter.)

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنَا لإِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾: He did not say "bawwaʾnā Ibrāhīma", though it is on a par with His saying ﴿وَلَقَدْ بَوَّأْنَا بَنِى إسْرائِيلَ مُبَوَّأَ صِدْقٍ﴾. If you wish, you treat ﴿بَوَّأنا﴾ as on a par with jaʿalnā ("We made"); that is how I heard it in the exegesis [Translator's note: the text has «الفسير», evidently for «التفسير»].
And if you wish, it is on a par with His saying ﴿قُلْ عَسَى أنْ يَكُونَ رَدِف لكم بعضُ﴾, whose meaning is "radifakum" ("has come close behind you"). All is correct.

farraa:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿يَأْتُوكَ رِجَالاً وَعَلَىٰ كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ يَأْتِينَ﴾: ﴿يأتينَ﴾ is the act of the she-camels. It has also [121 b] been read (يأتون), taking it to refer to the riders. Had He said "wa-ʿalā kulli ḍāmirin taʾtī", you would make it a singular verb, because (kull) is added to a singular. It is rare in the speech of the Arabs to say "I passed by every man, standing (qāʾimīna, plural)", yet it is correct. Stronger than it in permissibility is His saying ﴿فَمَا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حَاجِزِينَ﴾. The plural is permissible with aḥad and with kullu rajul only because their interpretation in the intention may be singular or plural. But when (aḥad) and kull separate [Translator's note: an individual] out of two, nothing but a singular verb for them is permissible. Of that is your saying "kullu rajulin minkumā qāʾimun" ("each man of you two is standing"); it is a mistake to say qāʾimūna or qāʾimāni, because the meaning has brought it back to the singular. Likewise "mā minkumā aḥadun qāʾimūna" or "qāʾimāni" is a mistake for that reason.

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُواْ تَفَثَهُمْ﴾ (the lām is quiescent), ﴿وَلْيُوفُواْ نُذُورَهُمْ وَلْيَطَّوَّفُواْ﴾: the lāms are quiescent. The people of Medina, ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash made them quiescent, while Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and al-Ḥasan gave them kasra, both after the wāw and elsewhere. Their making it quiescent is a lightening, as you say "wa-hwa qāla dhālika" and "wa-hya qālat dhāka", making the hāʾ quiescent when it is joined to the wāw. Likewise any lām of command joined to a wāw or a fāʾ: most of the speech of the Arabs makes it quiescent. Some of them gave kasra in ﴿ثُمَّ لِيَقْضُواْ﴾, because stopping on (ثُمَّ) is good, whereas it is not good on the fāʾ or the wāw. That is a valid option, except that most of the recitation makes the lām after thumma quiescent.
As for al-tafath, it is the slaughtering of the sacrificial camels and of other animals — cattle and sheep — the shaving of the head, the clipping of the nails, and the like.

farraa:30-30.t: His saying: ﴿وَأُحِلَّتْ لَكُمُ ٱلأَنْعَامُ إِلاَّ مَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ in Sūrat al-Māʾida: the strangled, the one beaten to death, the one killed by a fall, the one gored, to the end of the verse.

farraa:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿فَتَخْطَفُهُ ٱلطَّيْرُ﴾ is among the cases where yafʿalu has been referred back to faʿala. Had you put it in the accusative and said "fa-takhṭafahu al-ṭayru", it would have been a valid option. The Arabs sometimes give a response [Translator's note: with the fāʾ and the accusative] to kaʾannamā, because it has the sense of "it seems to me" and "I think", so it is as though it were referred back to the interpretation of (أنّ); do you not see that you say "it seems to me that you are going, so I will go (fa-adhhaba) with you"? Or, if you wish, you give (كأنَّما) the interpretation of a negation, as though you said: "As if you were an Arab, so that you would be honoured (fa-tukrama)", the interpretation being: "You are not an Arab, so that you would be honoured."

farraa:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿فَإِنَّهَا مِن تَقْوَى ٱلْقُلُوبِ﴾: He means "for the deed (al-faʿla)", as He said ﴿إنَّ رَبَّكَ مِنْ بَعْدِهَا لَغَفُورٌ رَحَيمٌ﴾, where "min baʿdihi" would also be permissible. Had it been said "fa-innahu min taqwā al-qulūb", it would have been permissible.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿لَكُمْ فِيهَا مَنَافِعُ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى﴾ means the sacrificial camels. He is saying: you may benefit from their milk and from riding them until they are designated or marked [Translator's note: as offerings]; that is the appointed term.
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ مَحِلُّهَآ إِلَىٰ ٱلْبَيْتِ ٱلْعَتِيقِ﴾: whatever is an offering for the ʿumra or for a vow is slaughtered when it reaches the House, and whatever is for the ḥajj is slaughtered at Minā. That was placed at Minā so that Mecca would be kept clean.
His saying: ﴿ٱلْعَتِيقِ﴾: it was freed from the tyrants. Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Ḥibbān narrated to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-ʿatīq: it was freed from the tyrants. And it is said: from the drowning in the time of Noah.

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْمُقِيمِي ٱلصَّلاَةِ﴾: you put (الصلاة) in the genitive when you dropped the nūn. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (والمقيمين الصلاةَ). Had you put (الصلاة) in the accusative while dropping the nūn, it would have been correct. One of them recited to me:
أسَيِّدُ ذو خُرَيِّطَةٍ نهاراً * من المتلقِّطى قَرَدَ القُمَامِ
(A little chief with a little bag by day, one of those who pick up the tangled scraps of the rubbish heaps.)
(and qaradi, genitive). The accusative with the nūn dropped is [122 a] permissible only because the Arabs say nothing but the accusative in the singular; they say "huwa al-ākhidhu ḥaqqahu" ("he is the one who takes his right"), putting al-ḥaqq in the accusative — they say nothing else — while the nūn is absent; so they built the dual and the plural on the singular and used the accusative with the nūn dropped. The proper way in the dual and the plural is the genitive, because their nūn may appear if you wish and be dropped if you wish, whereas in the singular it does not appear; therefore they used the accusative [Translator's note: there]. Had the genitive been used in the singular, that would have been permissible, but I have heard it only in their saying "huwa al-ḍāribu al-rajuli", for they put al-rajul in the genitive and in the accusative; whoever uses the genitive likens it to the manner of their saying "marartu bi-l-ḥasani al-wajhi" ("I passed by the one handsome of face"). When they put it in construct with a pronoun, they say "anta al-ḍāribuhu", "antumā al-ḍāribāhu" and "antum al-ḍāribūhu". The judgement on the hāʾ is that it is genitive in the singular, the dual and the plural; had you intended the accusative by it, it would have been a valid option, because the case-ending does not show in a pronoun. They took the opportunity of the construct because it connects with the genitive more closely than with the accusative, and so they took the stronger of the two ways in respect of connection. Whoever used the accusative ought to say "huwa al-ḍāribu iyyāhu", but I have not heard that.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿صَوَآفَّ﴾: hobbled. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (صَوافِنَ), meaning the standing ones. Al-Ḥasan read (صوافِىَ), saying: purely for Allah.
His saying: ﴿ٱلْقَانِعَ وَٱلْمُعْتَرَّ﴾: al-qāniʿ is the one who asks you (and accepts whatever you give him). Al-muʿtarr is one who is silent and puts himself in your way at the time of slaughter, but does not ask you.

farraa:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿لَن يَنَالَ ٱللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا﴾: they agreed on the yāʾ; had (تنال) been said, it would have been correct. The meaning of that is that the people of the Jāhiliyya, when they slaughtered them, would sprinkle the blood around the House. When the Muslims made the ḥajj, they wanted to do the same, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿لَن يَنَالَ ٱللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا وَلاَ دِمَآؤُهَا وَلَـٰكِن يَنَالُهُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ مِنكُمْ﴾: sincerity towards Him.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t: ﴿ثم ليقضوا تفثهم وليوفوا نذورهم وليطوفوا بالبيت العتيق﴾: ثم is a conjunction; the lām is the lām of command; يقضوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; تفثهم is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ليوفوا نذورهم﴾ is conjoined to ﴿يقضوا تفثهم﴾, and ﴿ليطوفوا بالبيت﴾ is likewise conjoined; بالبيت is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يطوفوا﴾; العتيق is an adjective (ṣifa) of البيت.

muyesser-irab:30-30.t:
﴿ذلك﴾: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the matter and the affair is that"; it is also said: a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "that is the matter which I have mentioned"; and it is also said: in the position of the accusative, its implied form being "comply with that".
﴿ومن يعظم حرمات الله فهو خير له عند ربه﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position. ﴿مَن﴾ is a jussive-inducing conditional noun, in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ; يعظم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), referring back to من; ﴿حرمات﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ; ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ and خير its khabar; ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) خير. The clause ﴿فهو خير﴾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the protasis together with its apodosis is the khabar of من. عند ربه: the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and ربه is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿وأحلت لكم الأنعام إلا ما يتلى عليكم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أحلت is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive); ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أحلت﴾; الأنعام is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); إلا is a particle of exception; ما is the excepted, in which both the connected and the disconnected (exception) are permissible: disconnected on the basis that what was mentioned in the verse of al-Māʾida is not of the genus of livestock, such as blood and the flesh of swine; and connected on the basis of referring it to such livestock as become forbidden through an incidental cause, such as death and the like. The clause يتلى is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent pronoun; ﴿عليكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يتلى﴾.
﴿فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان واجتنبوا قول الزور﴾: the fāʾ is a consequence drawn from His saying ﴿ومن يعظم حرمات الله﴾; اجتنبوا is an imperative verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; الرجس is the mafʿūl bihi; ﴿من الأوثان﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl, and it is also said: tamyīz (specification). واجتنبوا: the wāw is a conjunction, اجتنبوا is an imperative verb and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; قول الزور is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿اجتنبوا قول الزور﴾ is conjoined to the one before it.

muyesser-irab:31-31.t:
﴿حنفاء لله غير مشركين به﴾: حنفاء لله is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of اجتنبوا, and غير مشركين is likewise an emphasising ḥāl from it; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) مشركين.
﴿ومن يشرك بالله فكأنما خر من السماء فتخطفه الطير أو تهوي به الريح في مكان سحيق﴾: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position. من is a jussive-inducing conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يشرك بالله﴾ is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). فكأنما: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ; كأنما is the restraining (kāffa) and restrained (makfūfa) particle; خر is a past verb with a latent fāʿil (agent); من السماء is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خر﴾; فتخطفه is conjoined to خر, and الطير is the fāʿil. ﴿أو تهوي به الريح﴾: likewise conjoined; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تهوي﴾; في مكان is a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to ﴿تهوي﴾; سحيق is a naʿt (adjective) of مكان.

muyesser-irab:32-32.t:
﴿ذلك﴾: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the matter and the affair is that"; it is also said: a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "that is the matter which I have mentioned"; and it is also said: in the position of the accusative, its implied form being "comply with that".
﴿ومن يعظم شعائر الله فإنها من تقوى القلوب﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position. ﴿مَن﴾ is a jussive-inducing conditional noun, in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ; يعظم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), referring back to من; ﴿شعائر﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ. وإنها: إن is an abrogating particle (of inna and its sisters), and ﴿ها﴾ is its noun; ﴿من تقوى القلوب﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar of إن.

muyesser-irab:33-33.t: ﴿لكم فيها منافع إلى أجل مسمى ثم محلها إلى البيت العتيق﴾: لكم is a fronted khabar (predicate); فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); منافع is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿إلى أجل﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of منافع; مسمى is an adjective of أجل. ثم is a conjunction; محلها is a mubtadaʾ; إلى البيت is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar; العتيق is an adjective.

muyesser-irab:34-34.t:
﴿ولكل أمة جعلنا منسكا ليذكروا اسم الله على ما رزقهم من بهيمة الأنعام﴾: the wāw is resumptive; ﴿لكل أمة﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted, fronted second object of جعلنا; جعلنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); منسكًا is the first object of جعلنا; the clause ﴿ولكل أمة...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿ليذكروا﴾: the lām is the lām of causation; يذكروا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of causation; the interpreted maṣdar formed from أن and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿جعلنا﴾. ﴿اسم﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the Name of Majesty (Allah) is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿على ما رزقهم﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يذكروا﴾; the clause رزقهم is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; ﴿من بهيمة الأنعام﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿رزقهم﴾.
﴿فإلهكم إله واحد فله أسلموا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); ﴿إلهكم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), ﴿إله﴾ its khabar (predicate), and واحد an adjective (ṣifa). فله: the fāʾ is a conjunction; له is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أسلموا﴾. اسلموا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil. [Translator's note: the source spells it «اسلموا» without the hamza; the ayah has «أسلموا».]
﴿وبشر المخبتين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; بشر is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; المخبتين is the mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:35-35.t: ﴿الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم والصابرين على ما أصابهم والمقيمي الصلاة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون﴾: الذين is a naʿt (adjective) of المخبتين or a badal (substitute) from it. إذا is an adverb for future time, governing its protasis in the genitive and made accusative by its apodosis; the clause ﴿ذكر الله﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; the clause ﴿وجلت قلوبهم﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; إذا with its verb and its apodosis has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. الصابرين is conjoined to الذين; ﴿على ما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿الصابرين﴾; the clause أصابهم is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. المقيمي الصلاة is likewise conjoined, the nūn having been dropped because of the annexation. مما is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ينفقون﴾; the clause رزقناهم is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; and the clause ﴿مما رزقناهم ينفقون﴾ is conjoined to the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:36-36.t:
﴿والبدن جعلناها لكم من شعائر الله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; البدن is the object of an omitted verb, so it is accusative by way of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), i.e. "and We made the sacrificial camels"; جعلناها is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جعلناها﴾; ﴿من شعائر الله﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted second object of ﴿جعلناها﴾, which is in the sense of "making into".
﴿لكم فيها خير﴾: لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); خير is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or a ḥāl from the hāʾ in جعلناها.
﴿فاذكروا اسم الله عليها صواف﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); اذكروا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil; ﴿اسم﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi; عليها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿اذكروا﴾; صواف is a ḥāl from the hāʾ in عليها.
﴿فإذا وجبت جنوبها فكلوا منها وأطعموا القانع والمعتر﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; إذا is a future adverb, and the clause وجبت جنوبها is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. فكلوا: the fāʾ links the apodosis of إذا; the clause كلوا منها has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. وأطعموا القانع والمعتر: conjoined to the clause كلوا منها; أطعموا is a verb and its fāʿil; القانع is the mafʿūl bihi; and المعتر is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to القانع.
﴿كذلك سخرناها لكم لعلكم تشكرون﴾: كذلك: the kāf is a noun meaning "like", indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "He subjected them with a subjection like that subjection" [Translator's note: so in the source, «سخرها»; the ayah here has «سخرناها» (We subjected them); the wording seems carried over from the next ayah]; ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address. ﴿سخرناها﴾ is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is a ḥāl; ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿سخرناها﴾. لعلكم: لعل is an abrogating particle (of inna and its sisters), and ﴿كم﴾ is its noun; the clause تشكرون is the khabar of لعل, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the kāf in ﴿لكم﴾.

muyesser-irab:37-37.t:
﴿لن ينال الله لحومها ولا دماؤها ولكن يناله التقوى منكم﴾: لن: a particle of negation, of the accusative and of the future; ينال: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by لن; the Name of Majesty (Allah) is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); لحومها is the fāʿil (agent) of ينال; ولا دماؤها is conjoined to لحومها. ولكن: the wāw is a conjunction, and لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative because it is lightened; يناله is an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi; التقوى is the fāʿil; منكم is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from التقوى.
﴿كذلك سخرها لكم لتكبروا الله على ما هداكم﴾: ﴿كذلك﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like", indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "He subjected them with a subjection like that subjection"; ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address. سخرها is a past verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿سخرها﴾. لتكبروا: the lām is the lām of causation; تكبروا is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām of causation, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; the lām and what falls within its scope, a preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to ﴿سخرها﴾. The Name of Majesty is the mafʿūl bihi; على is a preposition, and ما is maṣdariyya, i.e. "for His guiding you", or relative, i.e. "for that to which He has guided you"; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿تكبروا﴾ because it is made to include the meaning of thanking.
﴿وبشر المحسنين﴾: the wāw is resumptive; بشر: an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; المحسنين is the mafʿūl bihi; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t:
﴿إن الله يدافع عن الذين آمنوا﴾: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position. إن الله: إن is an abrogating particle (of inna and its sisters), and the Name of Majesty (Allah) is its noun; the clause يدافع is the khabar of إن; عن الذين is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يدافع﴾; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of يدافع is omitted, its implied form being "the aggressions of the polytheists and their calamities".
﴿إن الله لا يحب كل خوان كفور﴾: a causal explanation of the preceding clause. إن الله: إن is an abrogating particle, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; the clause لا يحب is its khabar; كل خوان is the mafʿūl bihi; and كفور is an adjective (ṣifa) of خوان.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t:
﴿أذن للذين يقاتلون بأنهم ظلموا﴾: the clause is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position. أذن: a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive); what permission is given for is omitted because it is known, i.e. "permission is given to those who are fought, to fight". للذين is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أذن﴾; the clause يقاتلون is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; يقاتلون is an imperfect verb built for that whose agent is not named, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). بأنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to ﴿أذن﴾, the bāʾ being causal, i.e. "because of their being wronged". أنهم: أن and its noun, and the clause ظلموا is the khabar (predicate) of أنهم.
﴿وإن الله على نصرهم لقدير﴾: the wāw is resumptive. وإن الله: إن is an abrogating particle (of inna and its sisters), and the Name of Majesty (Allah) is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); قدير is the khabar of إن; على نصرهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to قدير; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:40-40.t:
﴿الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم بغير حق إلا أن يقولوا ربنا الله﴾: الذين is a naʿt (adjective) of, or a badal (substitute) from, ﴿الذين يقاتلون﴾, or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause أخرجوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; the wāw in ﴿أخرجوا﴾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); من ديارهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أخرجوا﴾; بغير حق is a ḥāl (circumstantial). إلا is a particle of exception, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from ﴿أن يقولوا﴾ is a disconnected excepted, accusative (manṣūb). It is also said: the exception is mufarragh (with the excepted-from left unexpressed), because of the presence of negation through غير, and ﴿أن يقولوا﴾ is in the position of the genitive as a badal from حق. ربنا is a mubtadaʾ and الله a khabar, and the clause ﴿ربنا الله﴾ is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض لهدمت صوامع وبيع وصلوات ومساجد يذكر فيها اسم الله كثيرا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position. لولا is a particle of non-occurrence due to occurrence, containing the meaning of condition; دفع الله is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is necessarily omitted; الناس is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of دفع, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its fāʿil (agent), which is Allah; بعضهم is a badal of part (badal baʿḍ) from الناس; ببعض is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿دفع﴾. The lām occurs in the apodosis of لولا; هدمت is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive); صوامع is the nāʾib fāʿil; ﴿وبيع وصلوات ومساجد﴾ is conjoined to صوامع; the clause يذكر is an adjective (ṣifa) of the places mentioned; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يذكر﴾; اسم الله is the nāʾib fāʿil; كثيرا is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "much remembrance", or an adjective of an omitted adverb of time, i.e. "much time".
﴿ولينصرن الله من ينصره﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position. The lām occurs in the response to an oath; ينصرن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the Name of Majesty (Allah) is the fāʿil; من is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi; and the clause ينصره is the ṣila of ﴿من﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿إن الله لقوي عزيز﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (of inna and its sisters), and the Name of Majesty is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); قوي is the first khabar of إن, and عزيز the second khabar of إن; the clause of إن and what follows it gives the cause of the help.

muyesser-irab:41-41.t:
﴿الذين إن مكناهم في الأرض أقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأمروا بالمعروف ونهوا عن المنكر﴾: الذين is a badal (substitute) from the preceding الذين; إن is conditional; مكناهم is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مكناهم﴾; أقاموا is a past verb and its fāʿil, and it is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); الصلاة is the mafʿūl bihi; and what follows is conjoined to it.
﴿ولله عاقبة الأمور﴾: the wāw is resumptive or a conjunction; لله is a fronted khabar (predicate), and عاقبة الأمور a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or conjoined.

muyesser-irab:42-42.t: ﴿وإن يكذبوك فقد كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح وعاد وثمود﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position. إن is conditional; يكذبوك is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). فقد: the fāʾ links the apodosis because it is joined to ﴿قد﴾; قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); كذبت is a past verb, and the tāʾ is the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine; the clause ﴿فقد كذبت﴾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); قبلهم is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كذبت﴾; قوم نوح is the fāʿil; and عاد وثمود: conjoined to قوم نوح.

muyesser-irab:43-43.t:
﴿وقوم إبراهيم﴾: conjoined to قوم نوح; the wāw is a conjunction, قوم is conjoined (maʿṭūf) and nominative (marfūʿ), and إبراهيم is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿وقوم لوط﴾: its i'rab is like the i'rab of وقوم إبراهيم.

muyesser-irab:44-44.t:
﴿وأصحاب مدين وكذب موسى﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أصحاب مدين is conjoined to قوم نوح; كذب is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive), and موسى is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
﴿فأمليت للكافرين ثم أخذتهم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; أمليت is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); للكافرين is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أمليت﴾; ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; أخذتهم is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿فكيف كان نكير﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as the fronted khabar of كان; نكير is the noun of كان.

muyesser-irab:45-45.t: ﴿فكأين من قرية أهلكناها وهي ظالمة فهي خاوية على عروشها وبئر معطلة وقصر مشيد﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; كأين is declarative (khabariyya, "how many"), and its position is the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); من قرية is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted tamyīz (specification) of كأين; the clause أهلكناها, made up of the verb, the fāʿil (agent) and the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), is the khabar (predicate) of كأين. ﴿وهي ظالمة﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; هي is a mubtadaʾ and ظالمة a khabar. The clause ﴿فكأين من قرية...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿وهي ظالمة﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). فهي: the fāʾ is a conjunction; هي is a mubtadaʾ and خاوية a khabar; the clause ﴿فهي خاوية﴾ is conjoined to the clause أهلكناها. على عروشها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خاوية﴾, the meaning being: fallen down upon their roofs, in that the roof fell first and then the walls collapsed upon it; or attached to an omitted second khabar of ﴿هي﴾, the meaning being: empty of their people, standing upon their roofs. بئر is conjoined to قرية, i.e. "and how many a well"; معطلة is an adjective (ṣifa) of بئر; قصر is likewise conjoined; and مشيد is an adjective of قصر.

muyesser-irab:46-46.t:
﴿أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فتكون لهم قلوب يعقلون بها أو آذان يسمعون بها﴾: the hamza is for interrogation; the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position. لم is a particle of negation, of inversion (to the past) and of the jussive; يسيروا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسيروا﴾. ﴿فتكون﴾: the fāʾ is causal, and ﴿تكون﴾ is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the causal fāʾ; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted fronted khabar of ﴿تكون﴾; قلوب is its postponed noun; the clause يعقلون is an adjective (ṣifa) of قلوب; ﴿بها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يعقلون﴾; أو is a conjunction; آذان is conjoined to قلوب; and the clause ﴿يسمعون بها﴾ is an adjective of آذان.
﴿فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار ولكن تعمى القلوب التي في الصدور﴾: the fāʾ is for causation; إن is an abrogating particle (of inna and its sisters), ﴿ها﴾ is its noun, and the clause ﴿لا تعمى الأبصار﴾ is the khabar. ولكن: the wāw is a conjunction, and لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), made inoperative because it is lightened; ﴿تعمى القلوب﴾ is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; التي is an adjective of القلوب; في الصدور is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:47-47.t:
﴿ويستعجلونك بالعذاب ولن يخلف الله وعده﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; يستعجلونك is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بالعذاب is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يستعجلونك﴾; the wāw is a conjunction; لن is a particle of negation and of the future; يخلف is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by لن; the Name of Majesty (Allah) is the fāʿil; and وعده is the mafʿūl bihi.
﴿وإن يوما عند ربك كألف سنة مما تعدون﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; إن is an abrogating particle (of inna and its sisters); يوما is the noun of إن; ﴿عند ربك﴾: the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿كألف﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like", indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إن; ﴿ألف﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi, and ﴿سنة﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿مما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of سنة; and the clause ﴿تعدون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:48-48.t: ﴿وكأين من قرية أمليت لها وهي ظالمة ثم أخذتها وإلي المصير﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; كأين is declarative (khabariyya, "how many"), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); من قرية is in the position of the accusative as the tamyīz (specification) of كأين; the clause ﴿أمليت لها﴾ is an adjective (ṣifa) of قرية. ﴿وهي﴾: the wāw is circumstantial, ﴿هي﴾ is a mubtadaʾ and ظالمة a khabar (predicate), and the clause ﴿وهي ظالمة﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ثم is a conjunction; أخذتها is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿أخذتها﴾ is conjoined to أمليت. وإليَّ: the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; ﴿إليَّ﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar; and المصير is a postponed mubtadaʾ. [Translator's note: the source names no khabar for كأين here.]
